item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky
item.stem:
Esha sketches the stars at 8 p.m. in January. In February she compares Earth’s night sky at 8 p.m. with the sky at 2 a.m. She is deciding whether Earth’s rotation on its axis or Earth’s revolution around the Sun explains the month-to-month change at the same clock time.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: The change from January’s 8 p.m. sky to February’s 8 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s revolution around the Sun.
options.B: The entire difference between January’s 8 p.m. sky and February’s 2 a.m. sky is caused by Earth’s revolution.
options.C: The change from January’s 8 p.m. sky to February’s 8 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s rotation on its axis.
options.D: Earth’s rotation and revolution are the same motion, so either word explains the February 8 p.m. change.
